title: Go When the Morning Shineth
description: Go When the Morning Shineth in Tonic Solfa to ANGEL'S STORY, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 97, “Pray Without Ceasing”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ANGEL'S STORY; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Go when the morn-ing shin-eth, Go when the noon is bright, Go when the eve de-cli-neth, Go in the hush of night; Go with pure mind and feel-ing, Put earth-ly thoughts a-way, And, in God's pre-sence kneel-ing, Do thou in se-cret pray.

lines: Go when the noon is bright,
Go in the hush of night;
Go with pure mind and feeling,
All who are loved by thee;
Pray, too, for those who hate thee,
Should holy thoughts come o'er thee
When friends are round thy way,
Will reach His throne of glory,
O, not a joy or blessing
The grace our Father gives us
To pour our souls in prayer:
His love who gave thee all.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ANGEL'S STORY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
